coaching.headline: Serath went eight kills and zero deaths, the team lost every detected fight, and two kills all game is barely a fucking pulse.
coaching.team: The team took the first Fangtooth, then lost all three detected fights and finished with two kills to the enemy's fourteen. Serath ran the game: eight kills, no deaths, the most objective damage and healing in the game, and every Steel death. The enemy took Mini Prime, the next Fangtooth, all three Seedlings and the only tower that fell. The only enemy hero to die was Riktor, twice, both times to TwinBlast.
coaching.lossReflection: The alternative was to stop handing Serath fights. The team's only kills landed on Riktor, and each was followed shortly by Serath killing TwinBlast. Treating a Riktor kill as the signal for the whole team to back off together, instead of staying for the next hit, aims to keep the trades from snowballing Serath. No plan guarantees a different result, but the current one gave Serath eight kills for zero deaths.

focus.title: Find Serath before the objective
focus.action: Before each Seedling, Fangtooth or Mini Prime, one player calls where Serath last showed. If nobody knows, the team gathers near Steel before anyone steps in. Next game, count how many team deaths land on the enemy jungler.

8.4.call: Greystone killed Scarlett, Serath killed Steel and Riktor killed Crunch in a 0-3 sequence, with a River objective going to the team in the same window. The record cannot show who engaged or whether those deaths were one fight.

11.7.call: TwinBlast killed Riktor at the same moment Serath killed Crunch, then Serath killed TwinBlast and Iggy & Scorch. The allied outer tower fell in that window, after Mini Prime had already gone and shortly before the enemy Fangtooth.

13.8.call: Neon killed Iggy & Scorch and TwinBlast killed Riktor within seconds, then Serath killed TwinBlast, Crunch and Steel. The enemy took a Seedling in the same window. A Riktor kill does not pay for three deaths to the same jungler.

matchup: Serath, the opposing jungler, was the bigger threat and killed Steel all three times.
Riktor's Skewer suppresses and Murdock's Long Arm of the Law ignores physical armor at unlimited range.
build: Xenia was the only completed item, and Heavy Metal turns its armor into extra magical damage.
Its shield only helps TwinBlast or Iggy & Scorch when Steel is close enough to touch.
eternal: With two takedowns, Cannibalism paid little.
Festering Wounds is the draft alternative to Regenerative Tissue: Steel's stuns would cut Serath's healing, giving up out-of-combat regeneration.
augment: Heavy Metal is fed by Xenia's armor.
Bulldozer is the peel-minded alternative, giving up armor-based damage for Bull Rush damage reduction.
Neither changes whether Steel is in range when Serath lands.
crest: Sanctification's tenacity has a clear purpose against Murdock's root, Serath's slows and the Crushing Descent stun.
Steel placed the most wards in the game.
improvement: With one completed item, nothing in this match proves the build cost a fight; Xenia is a sound keep.
The winning core adds Dynamo, which every Steel stun triggers, and Gaia Greaves against three physical damage dealers.

matchup: Greystone killed Scarlett once and never died, gaining armor and regeneration as health drops.
Serath brought the most healing in the game; respect Murdock's root and Riktor's suppress.
build: Tainted Blade was the team's only anti-heal, a direct answer to Greystone's regeneration and Serath's healing.
Nothing in the build adds armor against Greystone, Serath and Murdock.
eternal: With no kills or assists, Roses paid nothing this game.
Jealousy is the draft alternative to Roses: more damage as health falls, independent of takedowns, giving up the gold.
augment: Volcaic Slam's slow helps stick to Greystone or hold Serath near the team.
Scarlet Dawn is the alternative if First Intent's dash and shield matter more, giving up the slow.
crest: Liberator's cleanse has clear targets in Murdock's root, Neon's slows and the Data Burst mesmerize.
Whether it was available in the one death to Greystone is unknown.
improvement: Keep Tainted Blade as the team's anti-heal; Scarlett died once, so armor is not proven necessary.
If Greystone or Serath end exchanges before Swan Song lands, compare a physical armor item next, trading damage for staying in.

matchup: Serath killed TwinBlast both times, each shortly after a TwinBlast kill on Riktor.
Murdock finished with no deaths; Long Arm of the Law ignores all physical armor from unlimited range.
build: Mutilator was the only completed item; Vaporize and Vortex Grenade hits trigger its triple application.
Nothing in the build adds anti-heal or defense.
eternal: Melting Point adds damage only against heavily armored targets.
Sub-Surface, cutting area damage like Serath's Heresy and Neon's Data Burst, is the draft alternative to Melting Point for surviving dives.
augment: Grenadier means more slows while repositioning, helping open distance from Serath.
Amplified Burst is the alternative for safer Vaporize poke, giving up the extra grenade.
crest: Pacifier adds another escape beside Rocket Dash and Blink.
Whether the dash was available when Serath arrived is unknown.
improvement: Tainted Rounds is the clearest comparison: anti-heal on Serath, who had the most healing in the game.
It trades Mutilator's omnivamp, haste and maximum-health damage; Scarlett's Tainted Blade was the team's only anti-heal.
One completed item cannot prove a build cost a fight.

matchup: Neon took first blood outside any detected fight and got one more kill later.
Murdock got two kills on Iggy & Scorch outside any detected fight; Serath got one in the lost teamfight.
build: Dreambinder and Entropy suit a kit built on fire fields, turrets and oil.
Neither adds defense, and Iggy & Scorch has no dash beyond Blink.
eternal: This setup fits a hero who keeps enemies standing in fire.
Tithe of Death is the draft alternative to Lich, but with one takedown this game, Lich is the sound keep.
augment: Turret Maniac holds more space, but each turret breaks faster.
Hold This! is the alternative, trading turret count for ramping Molotov burst.
crest: Without a dash, Epoch only buys time, so it pays most when Steel is close.
Whether it was available in the deaths to Murdock and Neon is unknown.
improvement: With five deaths, sustain is the comparison: Orb Of Growth trades Dreambinder's health and slow for mana and cast healing.
The record cannot show which deaths a different item would have changed.

matchup: Serath finished with eight kills, no deaths and the most objective damage in the game.
Riktor killed Crunch once and Serath twice.
build: Berserker's Axe was the only completed item; Forward Crunch's dash triggers Blitz.
Nothing in the build adds armor against Serath, Murdock and Greystone.
eternal: Crunch took the most damage on the team, so Prima Donna's downside applied to every hit.
Immaculate, damage reduction near full health, is the draft alternative to Prima Donna.
augment: Lunge Crunch lets stun engages and escapes start from farther away.
Combo Crunch is the alternative, trading reach for sustained damage.
crest: Iceskorn Talons is a group-fight tool rather than a personal escape; its value depends on teammates fighting on the sheet.
improvement: Salvation, from the winning core, is the most direct survival comparison against Serath.
No armor against three physical damage dealers, but one completed item cannot show what a different second item would change.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs did the support paperwork: a hand in both team kills, the most wards placed in the game, the team's only ward cleared and the most damage mitigated on the team.

Serath killed Steel all three times, twice before the ten-minute mark, like a tank-shaped piñata. Heaven's Fury makes Serath immune to crowd control mid-dash, so hold Bull Rush or Shield Bash until Serath reappears on a teammate.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster died once, the fewest on the team, in a game where the team died fourteen times, with farm right on the recorded Scarlett norm. Keep that discipline.
No kills, no assists and hero damage a quarter under the recorded Scarlett norm is a lantern with no flame. When Serath lands on a teammate, Swan Song goes on Serath.
64df5e4c-dd6b-4648-8f09-99bc06a06ff8: Rain_Gaup scored both team kills, both on Riktor, and died only twice, well under the recorded TwinBlast norm. In a two-kill game, the carry was the only one drawing blood.

Serath killed TwinBlast shortly after each Riktor kill, and a support kill is worth fuck all when the carry dies right after. When Serath reappears on TwinBlast, Vortex Grenade slows Serath and Rocket Dash heads toward Steel.
f647bbff-e974-4ef9-9899-1cde1163a946: Aqua led the team in hero damage, second in the whole game, and farmed above the recorded Iggy & Scorch norm. The damage rate still sat well under that norm.

Five deaths, the most in the game, is a fucking donation drive: three outside any detected fight, two to Murdock. When Murdock or Neon is missing from the map, Iggy & Scorch plays behind turrets near Steel.
177c1537-65a7-4e57-b342-2ea4298a9092: Pinkigh led the team in objective damage and healing. But no kills, no assists and the lowest hero damage in the game is a jungler bringing a pillow to a knife fight.
Serath killed Crunch twice, once in the lost teamfight shortly before the enemy Fangtooth. Once Serath is ahead, Crunch only takes a fight with Steel or Scarlett close enough to follow.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~2.5s of lockdown): Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Crunch Right Crunch (knockup 1.25s), Iggy & Scorch Inferno (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.playAgainst: peel/CC him off — without resets he's stranded; anti-heal blunts Re-Crunch

ourKits.winCondition: layer fire zones on a choke/objective and burn the team
ourKits.playWith: CC that holds enemies in his fire
ourKits.playAgainst: don't fight in his zones — flank; kill the turret, dive him

enemyKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
enemyKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

enemyKits.winCondition: pull a target in and chain silence+suppress for a guaranteed kill
enemyKits.playWith: burst that deletes his pulled/suppressed target
enemyKits.playAgainst: respect Riplash range — stay spaced; cleanse/QSS the suppress

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

enemyKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
enemyKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

loadout.plain: Attack faster, heal from all damage, and add damage to each hit for 6s. Pop it alongside Heresy for a burst of fast, healing on-hit attacks.

worked.eternalPart: The Eternal was part of it: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity) sits on the same triggers as the items (every basic attack set off; healing off the damage), so the same hits paid out twice.

countered.text: 1 of the 4 players Serath killed built physical armor (Steel).

copy.text: Thraex (Savage Strikes + Ferocity): 46.9% in 1,276 Serath jungle games, below the hero's 49.7%. It wins less than usual elsewhere: it beat us, not the field.

loadout.name: Ghost in the Machine
loadout.text: After dashing with Erase Vector, become invisible for 1s.

ability.name: Erase Vector
ability.what: Dash in the current movement direction, Empowering your next Jolt within 3s to explode, dealing 60/85/110/135/160 (+40%) bonus Magical Damage to the target and nearby enemies as well as Slowing them by 20% for 0.5s.

loadout.plain: Dashing with Erase Vector turns Neon invisible for 1s, so enemies lose sight of her while she repositions before the empowered Jolt.

loadout.name: Aion
loadout.text: Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.
loadout.plain: Each cast adds mana regen and ability damage to heroes earns gold. Neon casts constantly to build Threads, so this keeps her mana and gold flowing.

loadout.name: Bottomless Vial
loadout.text: Killing a River Buff restores a Potion charge and grants +5 Magical Power permanently.
loadout.plain: Taking a river buff refills a potion and grants permanent magic power. A jungle or roaming habit, not tied to her abilities.

loadout.name: Runic Focus
loadout.text: Gain 0.2% increased Magical Power per 1% current Mana.
loadout.plain: More magic power while Neon's mana bar is high. Rewards poking from full mana instead of spending it all at once.

loadout.name: Soulbearer
loadout.text: Anima:  Gain a 100 (+35) (+6%) Shield for 8s. Gain 20% Magical Lifesteal and 10% Movement Speed for 8s.
loadout.plain: Activate for a shield, healing off magic damage and speed. Use it with Final Thread so the Overclocked burst heals her back up.

lines: Lead story: Hard to kill. Never died in 15 minutes, fewer deaths than about 95% of Neon mid players this patch. The build added health and armor and healing off damage.
Final Thread at rank 2: 110s base, about 82.7s by the end (25% shorter) from 33 ability haste: Azure Core 10, Oathkeeper 15, Soulbearer 8.
Neon dealt 10,628 hero damage, 28% of their team's, with +180 magical power from items.
Oathkeeper (item): On Ability Cast: Empower your next Basic Attack within 4s. Deal 65 (+35%) Damage On-Hit.
Aion (Eternal): Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.

Sustain: Azure Core: On going below 40% Health: Gain a 100 (+12%) Shield for 5s.; Soulbearer: Gain a 100 (+35) (+6%) Shield for 8s. Gain 20% Magical Lifesteal and 10% Movement Speed for 8s.; 1,410 healing recorded.
Toughness: +175 health; took 6,786 damage, mitigated 4,044, died 0 times.

Loadout augment Ghost in the Machine: Dashing with Erase Vector turns Neon invisible for 1s, so enemies lose sight of her while she repositions before the empowered Jolt. (game text: After dashing with Erase Vector, become invisible for 1s.) (changes Erase Vector, 9s cooldown with their haste) Field: 48.5% in 1014 games, 34% of picks, level the hero-role's 48.6%.

Loadout Eternal Aion: Each cast adds mana regen and ability damage to heroes earns gold. Neon casts constantly to build Threads, so this keeps her mana and gold flowing. (game text: Casting a spell grants 1 Mana Regeneration for 8s (stacks 5x). Spells also grant gold equal to 6% of damage dealt to Enemy Heroes.) Field: 49.2% in 777 games, 26% of picks, level the hero-role's 48.6%.

Loadout minor Bottomless Vial: Taking a river buff refills a potion and grants permanent magic power. A jungle or roaming habit, not tied to her abilities. (game text: Killing a River Buff restores a Potion charge and grants +5 Magical Power permanently.) Field: 51% in 494 games, 64% of picks, above the hero-role's 48.6%.

Loadout minor Runic Focus: More magic power while Neon's mana bar is high. Rewards poking from full mana instead of spending it all at once. (game text: Gain 0.2% increased Magical Power per 1% current Mana.) Field: 50.3% in 388 games, 50% of picks, above the hero-role's 48.6%.

Loadout crest Soulbearer: Activate for a shield, healing off magic damage and speed. Use it with Final Thread so the Overclocked burst heals her back up. (game text: Anima:  Gain a 100 (+35) (+6%) Shield for 8s. Gain 20% Magical Lifesteal and 10% Movement Speed for 8s.) Field: 53.4% in 706 games, 23% of picks, above the hero-role's 48.6%.
Countered? 0 of the 1 players Neon killed built magical armor. We killed Neon 0 times.
Copy it? Aion (Bottomless Vial + Runic Focus): 49.6% in 284 Neon midlane games, above the hero's 48.6%. Proven this patch: worth copying.

card.lesson: Final Thread came back about every 83s instead of 110s by the end (25% shorter). Count it, and take fights while it is down.
